outcome.reason: all critical claims are tied to collected evidence

The incident was resolved by remediating the faulty CoreDNS configuration in the kube-system/coredns ConfigMap and executing a safe rollout restart of the CoreDNS deployment. CoreDNS had been configured with a custom forwarding stanza for bench.proofix:53 pointing to the faulty upstream resolver proofix-dns-bad (10.43.98.165:5353), which introduced latency and NXDOMAIN errors for dependent workloads. The ConfigMap was patched to revert to the known-good Corefile configuration, and the CoreDNS deployment rollout restart completed successfully.

The incident in CASE-11 was caused by the orders-consumer Deployment in namespace proofix-case-11 being scaled down from 3 replicas to 1 replica. With 6 topic partitions and an ingress rate of 42 records/second (with ~0.04s processing time per record), a single consumer replica was saturated at 25 records/second, causing continuous consumer lag growth. The deployment has been restored by scaling orders-consumer back to 3 replicas, enabling parallel partition consumption across the group to drain and bound consumer lag.
